executiveSummary: GM0654 has coherent 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, exact deterministic allocation, complete ten-preset/T+0-72 execution, explicit evidence classes and non-causal public context. It is not locally releasable for Borsele operations: a generic coastal scalar is presented without a selected Westerschelde defence/event footprint, the Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset creates sustained local flood stress, unrelated hazards share one neighbourhood ordering, and the model omits an authority-reviewed Borssele nuclear/industrial-release pathway. Seven road-border proxies are reused by all eight services and cannot represent the N62/Westerscheldetunnel approach, Sloe/Borssele power nodes, water/drainage assets, rural facilities or operator restoration. These are correction blockers, not evidence of a current incident, unsafe dike, grid outage or nuclear release.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: A fresh official GM0654 row gives Borsele, 23,125 residents, density 163 per square kilometre, 5,275 residents aged 65+ and 3,091 one-person households.

The generated municipality values and all 32 official neighbourhood records use this 2025 table; published rounded or suppressed values remain source context rather than individual vulnerability, present occupancy or hazard exposure.

The API is machine-readable and reusable under CC BY 4.0. CBS labels the table 2025 data and adds source variables as they become available; an edition/snapshot timestamp must be pinned for replay. Null is unavailable, never an observed zero.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / CBS / Kadaster / Rijkswaterstaat / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: CBS Gebiedsindelingen 2025 and integration-ready national reference OGC services
supports: Fresh non-generalized GM0654 has three components, three rings and 7,703 positions. The overview polygon retains three components/three rings with 148 positions; RD shoelace estimates are 142.776 and 142.704 square kilometres, a -0.050% overview difference.

The generated centre is contained. All 15 BAG woonplaats records retain official GM0654 membership; the independently versioned label centres for Ellewoutsdijk and Hoedekenskerke lie outside both CBS outlines, so containment failure is a source/edition caveat rather than evidence that either place belongs elsewhere.

CBS boundary OGC is annual/CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark 1.0. RWS NWB OGC is monthly/CC0 1.0 and a daily Public Domain GeoPackage also exists. These are reference geometry, not current closures, evacuation throughput or utility routes.

HWH IMWA/DAMO OGC services are CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor timestamps and variable completeness. The current app intersection contains 116 points: 16 sewer pumps, 12 surface-water pumps, one sluice and 87 weirs. Registers do not prove hydraulic connectivity, capacity units/control, current operation, emergency power or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaattest Borsele — quick scan van kwetsbaarheden en oplossingen
evidenceSources.edition: 21 December 2017 quick scan, checked against municipality 2024 accountability material
supports: The municipality identifies the south as most flood-vulnerable, especially Hoedekenskerke and recreation area Scheldeoord at Baarland; it describes vulnerable access to the Westerscheldetunnel, A58/N-road evacuation limits, inner dikes, the 's-Gravenpolder pump and Evides assets near Nieuwdorp.

Named pluvial areas include east Hoedekenskerke, northwest Heinkenszand/Slaakweg, Lancaster in Nieuwdorp, Scheldeoord, the Sloeweg/Bernardweg junction and the Heinkenszand-Nieuwdorp agricultural area. It explicitly says further model research is needed, including for KCB and Sloe industry.

The report distinguishes heat in care/education uses and the hardened Sloe area, drought/salinisation along the Westerschelde and agricultural fresh-water scarcity, and flood cascades through power, telecom, drinkwater, industry and mobility.

This is fixed expert/policy evidence, not a live sensor feed or validated 2026 exposure raster. No stable machine export, grid resolution, standard reuse licence or contractual refresh cadence is published; the 2017 local findings require owner review before causal ingestion.

evidenceSources.title: Dijkversterking Zak van Zuid-Beveland and public water-system ArcGIS services
evidenceSources.edition: Current project page and 2025 water-board regulation service
supports: Approximately 16 kilometres across 19 sections between KCB Borssele and Hansweert require strengthening to meet future standards; the water board explicitly says this does not mean the dike is acutely unsafe. Exploration is 2024-2026, plan development 2027-2028 and realization is planned for 2029-2033.

The integration-ready EXT_ALG_DSO_2025 FeatureServer at https://geo.scheldestromen.nl/arcgis/rest/services/Extern/EXT_ALG_DSO_2025/FeatureServer covers the full water-board area in EPSG:28992 and exposes primary/regional defences, protection zones, watercourses, water bodies, roads and pump protection as queryable JSON/GeoJSON/PBF.

EXT_WK_Waterkeringen also exposes defence/reference objects. These legal/physical objects can select and explain a reach but are not live condition, failure probability, breach, surge, depth, arrival or dewatering performance.

The DSO service is explicitly the 2025 regulation edition. The public service directory states no standard reuse licence or contractual refresh cadence; record those as unknown and obtain publisher approval before caching or causal use.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Watermanagementcentrum Nederland / Provincie Zeeland / KNMI
evidenceSources.title: Waterinfo, LIWO, Zeeland flood-scenario OGC and KNMI event-forcing data
supports: LIWO is the professional planning system for flood maps and requires specialist interpretation; its named scenarios can expose maximum depth, flow, rise, warning/arrival and related exercise information. A layer/event/version must be selected before it can drive an exercise.

Province Zeeland publishes protected and unprotected maximum-depth WMS/WFS through https://opengeodata.zeeland.nl/geoserver/water/ under Public Domain terms. These are static scenario indications with layer-specific resolution/probability and no stated guaranteed refresh interval, not observed depth or current failure.

Waterinfo provides parameter/location-specific current and historical Westerschelde water, wave and wind observations. KNMI Data Platform provides file/product-valid weather and radar data, commonly 5- or 10-minute products, under CC BY 4.0. Both may support a named replay with issue/valid time; neither supplies a generic deterministic T+72 forecast or inundation result.

The application still exposes ROR second-cycle 2016-2021 risk areas with no planned refresh and clearly labels them as screening. That public context must not be silently promoted into the coastal scalar.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Crisisplan Zeeland 2026-2029 and public Borssele nuclear preparedness boundaries
evidenceSources.edition: VRZ crisis plan 2026-2029; current national and operator pages
supports: The current VRZ plan explicitly routes a nuclear incident at Borssele or Doel to the separate Algemeen Rampenbestrijdingsplan Stralingsincidenten, distinguishes tactical/operational plans from the public strategic framework, includes Belgian cross-border coordination and is re-adopted at least every four years.

Rijksoverheid states Borssele preparedness includes iodine distribution for defined 0-20 and 20-100 kilometre target groups; iodine is taken only on government advice. Depending on severity, wind and precipitation, protective measures can include sheltering, evacuation up to 10 kilometres, and food/drinking-water controls.

EPZ's public cybersecurity explanation states vital control systems are not internet-connected, reactor control is largely analogue/direct and supporting ICT is not used for emergency control decisions. Therefore the generic cyber preset must not imply nuclear process-control failure.

These are authoritative fixed preparedness/scope statements, not an observed release, source term, plume, dose, protective-action decision, resource inventory or live KCB state. No reviewed public machine API, standard licence or refresh contract supplies those restricted operational elements; retain them unknown or use an authority-reviewed, explicitly synthetic exercise.

evidenceSources.title: REV public WMS/WFS and API for regulated external-safety activities and attention areas
supports: The integration-ready national WFS https://rev-portaal.nl/geoserver/wfs?request=GetCapabilities exposes full features for regulated activities, pipelines/Basisnet and fire, explosion and toxic-cloud attention areas; WMS supports map display.

A fresh bbox query around GM0654 returned named Nieuwdorp/Sloe-area records including Seveso, ammonia refrigeration, gas storage, wind-turbine and terminal activities with record registration times; the bbox also intersects neighbouring municipalities and is not itself a municipality count.

The application correctly requests REV as visible external-safety context with affectsSimulation=false and warns that activity/attention-area presence is not a release, damage report, plume, probability or scenario impact.

REV records have per-feature registration/validity metadata, but the public map-service page states no fixed feed cadence or reuse-licence version. Preserve record timestamps, source-holder fields and unknown/no-value reasons, and never interpret absent features as zero risk.

evidenceSources.publisher: TenneT / Stedin / Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland
evidenceSources.title: Borssele-Sloe electricity infrastructure, projects and public distribution-grid geometry
evidenceSources.edition: 2026 project decision and current operator open-data pages
supports: The official project decision describes the existing Borssele 380 kV station as physically full after IJmuiden Ver Alpha and plans a new 380 kV Nieuwdorp-Liechtensteinweg station connected to Borssele-Rilland, 150 kV works and Nederwiek 1. This is project/reference context, not current failure or spare capacity at T+24.

Stedin publishes downloadable SHP geometry for low-, medium- and high-voltage connections/stations in its service area, refreshed at least annually after year end with a stated snapshot in the metadata. The page does not state a standard open licence and warns it is indicative, not a KLIC substitute or operational decision source.

Stedin's current Zeeland congestion page and RVO/TenneT project pages show regional capacity constraints and expansion, but they do not expose public live switching, load flow, outage, backup, black-start or restoration topology.

Public geometry may safely establish provider/asset context and service-specific aggregate zones. Security-sensitive connectivity, live state and repair commitments must remain unknown or be supplied through an authorized safe aggregate interface, never inferred from seven road edges.

identity.summary: GM0654, Borsele, Zeeland and safety region Zeeland are internally and officially coherent.
notes: pnpm audit:context -- GM0654 confirmed code/name, province, exactly one safety region and a generated centre inside both overview and fresh non-generalized geometry.
Boundary and statistics editions are 2025; the region bundle contains only GM0654 neighbourhoods and places.
VRZ's current plan supplies the responsible response-region context and explicitly addresses Borssele nuclear coordination.

geography.summary: Municipal topology and area are coherent, but the 148-position overview boundary cannot resolve Westerschelde reaches, flood compartments, low points, access roads or assets.
notes: Fresh full-resolution and generated overview geometry both retain three components/three rings; the approximate overview-area difference is only -0.050%.
Full-resolution geometry has 7,703 positions versus 148 and is mandatory for dike, raster, road, drainage and asset intersections.
South Borsele/Westerschelde, Sloe industry, villages, rural polders and elevated evacuation/refuge areas are distinct mechanisms that a single municipality coordinate cannot assign.

demography.summary: Generated municipality totals reproduce official 2025 CBS values and published neighbourhood population reconciles exactly.
notes: Official/generated population is 23,125, density 163/km², age 65+ is 5,275 or 22.8%, and one-person households total 3,091.
Published neighbourhood population sums to 23,125 and households to 9,910; rounded neighbourhood age-65-plus values sum to 5,280, five above the municipality value.
Resident statistics exclude Sloe workers, school/care occupancy, campground/recreation visitors and evacuees; no timestamped present-population feed is consumed.

regionalDetail.summary: All 32 official neighbourhoods and non-residential activity context are retained, but gaps and a shared seed prevent operational exposure assignment.
notes: All 32 neighbourhoods expose the expected 36 source fields. Cars per household is available for 27/32; district-heating share and public charging points are unavailable for all 32 and correctly remain null.

Havengebied Sloe Nieuwdorp has zero residents but 88 non-residential buildings, 40 businesses and 928 hectares; the applied activity-demand logic correctly avoids interpreting zero residents as zero service activity.
CBS aggregates and REV/register locations do not define present workers, individual vulnerability, flood/heat/release exposure, operational priority or safe restoration.

settlements.summary: Fifteen BAG woonplaatsen and 28 BRT settlement labels are represented, with two independently versioned BAG label-point containment caveats.
notes: The BAG woonplaatsen include all 15 named villages listed in the region context; settlement labels are not substituted for neighbourhoods or flood compartments.

Ellewoutsdijk and Hoedekenskerke BAG label centres fall outside both the generalized and 2025 non-generalized CBS boundary, while their source records retain municipalityCode GM0654. Do not rewrite membership from cross-source point containment.
Recreation areas, Sloe work sites and sparse rural presence are not measured by settlement labels.

transport.summary: Road/stop reference coverage is broad, but it cannot reproduce N62/tunnel-approach, rural evacuation, transit or lifeline constraints.
notes: Seven logical links connect N254 to Vlissingen, N62 to Terneuzen/Goes, A58/N665/N669 to Goes and N666 to Kapelle; nominal capacities are 150 scenario units except A58 at 260.

There is no ProRail passenger station in GM0654. Sixty GTFS stop areas improve village discovery but provide no passengers, vehicle availability/accessibility, real-time service, evacuation role or throughput.

Municipal evidence distinguishes a likely dry Westerscheldetunnel from vulnerable approaches and warns about A58/N-road access. The model has no explicit approach segment, flood closure, evacuation destination, contraflow, vertical refuge or rural pickup logic.

emergencyContext.summary: Public flood, nuclear, industrial, water, facility and grid context is visible, but defining Borsele mechanisms do not drive the ten exercises.
notes: The app intersection contains 116 water objects, 14 government-service points, zero RIVM acute-care locations and 20 DUO education uses. These correctly remain official context rather than invented capacity.
REV regulated-activity/attention layers are visible and explicitly non-causal; no selected industrial release, toxic plume, fire/explosion footprint or protective-action area enters the model.

KCB Borssele and national/VRZ protective-action mechanisms are absent from the ten presets. Operator control, source term, dose, shelter/evacuation decision and live resource data remain unavailable or restricted and must not be fabricated.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six checkpoints across all eight services with finite output, but execution completeness does not establish local validity.
notes: The initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0654 pnpm audit:model run passed one file/two tests in 27.41 seconds (27.23 seconds tests). The mandatory final current-code rerun also passed one file/two tests in 28.42 seconds (28.22 seconds tests), and a focused reproduction passed.

The remaining values are winter 0.496832 / 7,697 / 259,121.473; cyber 0.455431 / 8,791 / 310,451.612; remote Groningen earthquake 0.000770 / 0 / 691.977; remote wildfire/smoke/drought 0.105151 / 0 / 71,267.357; compound 0.866688 / 16,436 / 870,559.856.

At coastal T+24 the raw dimensionless derived-screening inundation stress is 1.694148, gust is 27.2415 m/s, affected people-equivalent is 12,409 and drainage availability is 0.135144. This is not 1.694 metres, a current breach or a forecast.

At compound T+24, rain is 52.6929 mm/h, standing-water stress 0.386528, gust 29.7725 m/s and cyber disruption 0.399549; 14,168 people-equivalent are affected. Weather, cyber, earthquake and fire presets are deterministic exercises unless bound to an explicit replay.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact-zero semantics, local allocation, reconciliation, cumulative burden and layer invariance pass.
notes: All eight availability values stay in [0,1]; hazard dimensions, demand, delivery, affected people-equivalent and attributable person-hours are finite and non-negative at all 60 preset/checkpoint combinations.
For every preset/checkpoint, intensity zero yields exactly zero current/peak event severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours.
Compound T+24 has 32 rows for every service, summing to 23,125 residents and 14,168 affected people-equivalent; all demand/delivery totals reconcile with maximum floating discrepancy about 1.78e-15.

Repeated frames are deterministic, cumulative attributable burden never decreases, route flow respects effective capacity, and every selectable layer leaves hazard, pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One shared neighbourhood seed overrides Borsele's documented flood, pluvial, heat and industrial geography.
notes: At T+24 pluvial, coastal, heat and wildfire have exactly the same 32-neighbourhood order. Kern Ovezande, Buitengebied Nieuwdorp, Kern Lewedorp and Kern 's-Heerenhoek lead; the same order repeats across unrelated mechanisms.

The municipal quick scan instead differentiates south Borsele/Hoedekenskerke/Scheldeoord flood exposure, named pluvial low points, Sloe heat/drought and distinct power/water/access assets. Sloe/Borssele/Ellewoutsdijk positions cannot be derived from the shared seed.

The coastal scalar is based on simplified coast proximity and selects no Scheldestromen reach, hydraulic connection, breach, surge, depth cell, arrival or recession. No local fire footprint is modeled; the canonical wildfire is a remote exercise with zero direct flame in GM0654.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight coherent service balances are computed, but identical road proxies replace sector topology and Borsele-specific cross-sector dependencies.
notes: Coastal T+24 availability is power 0.605326, water 0.409633, drainage 0.135144, gas 0.660125, telecom 0.261704, mobility 0.150628, facilities 0.709153 and supply 0.747721.
Compound T+24 availability is power 0.628130, water 0.185383, drainage 0.141208, gas 0.417756, telecom 0.119363, mobility 0.431636, facilities 0.663478 and supply 0.636334.

Every service exposes the same seven N/A58/N-road IDs with transferSemantics logical-proxy. Flow differs, but no official source establishes those roads as power, drinking-water, drainage, gas, telecom or facility-transfer edges.

The app's official water, REV and grid layers can scope assets/provider context but not connectivity, live state, capacity, backup or restoration. Sloe zero-resident activity demand is correctly retained, yet it is distributed without physical KCB/industrial/energy or facility interfaces.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality ledgers close, and the UI visibly separates official context from simulated consequences.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity; each service baseline plus ordered stage deltas sums to availability; the eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality pressure. Dependency, intervention and counterfactual values are finite.

Preparedness changes modeled consequences after physical pressure rather than changing hazard fragility. Exact no-event reruns and proportional dimension attribution are labelled by method/evidence class.

At Borsele coastal T+24 the browser displays 'Scenario · evidence class derived-screening' and explicitly says ROR/HWH/REV layers are registers/screens, not a selected breach, depth, arrival, performance or incident impact.

A 1440x1000 headless Chromium path loaded without page, console or local-response errors, selected Borsele, coastal T+24 and Kern Hoedekenskerke by map click. Initial readiness was 1.043 s, municipality selection 0.063 s, scenario 0.214 s, checkpoint 0.950 s and drilldown 0.713 s; timings are diagnostics, not hazard evidence.

recovery72h.summary: Standing water correctly pauses repair, but coastal recession, facility depletion and every operator restoration magnitude remain uncalibrated.
notes: Compound retains 0.386528 standing-water stress and 0.051965 cyber disruption at T+72, remains critical with 16,436 affected people-equivalent and keeps recoveryProgress at zero for all eight services.

Coastal direct water/wind forcing is zero at T+72, yet 5,224 remain modeled under pressure. Availability ranges from facilities 0.314875 to gas 0.879064 and modeled recovery ranges 0.461925-0.932474 without a selected event, dewatering/access or operator repair plan.

Coastal facilities fall from 0.709153 at T+24 to 0.314875 at T+72; compound facilities fall from 0.663478 to 0.166170. These deterministic reserve/dependency results are not evidence about any named school, care site, shelter or KCB facility.

Storm, pluvial, winter, earthquake and wildfire direct forcing ends by T+72 without reducing cumulative attributable person-hours; heat, river, cyber/compound follow preset schedules. Exact-zero and sustained-flood fixes work, but local recovery percentages are unverified.

findings.summary: Official identity, 2025 population and all 32 neighbourhood records are coherent; null and non-residential activity semantics are preserved.
findings.evidence: Fresh CBS gives 23,125 residents and the neighbourhood sum is exactly 23,125. All 36 fields are exposed, district-heating/charging gaps remain null, and zero-resident Sloe areas can receive separate activity demand rather than being treated as empty infrastructure.
findings.action: Keep CBS/PDOK edition, retrieval, licence and suppression metadata pinned; retain null != zero and resident != present-worker/visitor semantics in every export.

findings.summary: Two BAG place label centres do not pass point containment against either CBS boundary edition.
findings.evidence: Ellewoutsdijk and Hoedekenskerke label centres are outside both overview and fresh non-generalized 2025 GM0654 geometry, while BAG records explicitly retain municipalityCode GM0654; all other 13 centres pass.
findings.action: Preserve authoritative source membership and surface the cross-source geometry caveat. Never reassign places from generalized or independently versioned label-point containment.

findings.summary: The high-consequence coastal result has no selected Westerschelde defence failure or flood scenario.
findings.evidence: Coastal produces dimensionless raw inundation stress 1.694148, 12,409 affected at T+24, 14,444 peak and 813,236.197 attributable person-hours by T+72 from coast proximity. Scheldestromen identifies a specific approximately 16 km future strengthening project and explicitly says it is not acutely unsafe; the model selects no reach, event, probability, depth/arrival/recession or dewatering state.
findings.action: Suppress direct local coastal depth/exposure as unsupported until a water-authority-reviewed, versioned LIWO/Zeeland event is intersected with full-resolution GM0654 and an explicit Scheldestromen reach/state. Never convert the strengthening programme into a current breach.

findings.summary: The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset creates sustained direct flood stress in Borsele despite the wrong named source system.
findings.evidence: The preset yields flood stress 0.406828 at T+24 and T+72, up to 1,750 affected and 250,337.233 attributable person-hours. Borsele's local large-water source is tidal Westerschelde/coastal and regional polder water; the scenario does not establish a Rhine, Meuse or IJssel hydraulic pathway.
findings.action: Require named-source hydraulic connectivity before direct river forcing. For GM0654 set the canonical major-river direct footprint to unsupported/zero as appropriate, while keeping separately named Westerschelde coastal and regional-water exercises.

findings.summary: A shared neighbourhood seed makes unrelated hazards spatially identical and contradicts named Borsele hotspots.
findings.evidence: Pluvial, coastal, heat and wildfire repeat exactly the same T+24 ranking, led by Kern Ovezande. Municipal evidence instead distinguishes Hoedekenskerke/Scheldeoord flooding, specific pluvial low points, hardened Sloe heat/drought, Westerschelde salinisation and asset/access locations.
findings.action: Replace the shared seed with hazard-specific intersections using full-resolution boundaries, owner-reviewed local stress layers, LIWO/Zeeland event grids, AHN/BGT covariates and combustible-land eligibility; preserve no-data as unknown and test that independent hazards no longer clone ranks.

findings.summary: The canonical set omits Borsele nuclear/radiological and Sloe industrial-release exercises and leaves a dangerous cyber interpretation gap.
findings.evidence: VRZ explicitly plans for KCB Borssele/Doel nuclear incidents, national guidance distinguishes wind/precipitation-dependent shelter, evacuation, iodine and food/water measures, and REV exposes multiple Sloe regulated activities. None drives a source term, plume, protective action, exposure or service pathway. EPZ states vital/reactor control is isolated and largely analogue, so generic cyber service disruption is not nuclear control failure.
findings.action: Add authority-reviewed, separately named radiological and industrial-release exercises or clearly exclude them from scope. Use REV only to select context, KNMI only for event-valid meteorology, and public protective-action rules as policy context; source term, dose, decisions and restricted operational data must come from authorities or a conspicuously synthetic versioned case.

findings.summary: Seven road-border proxies are cloned across all services and omit the defining rural/tunnel access topology.
findings.evidence: Every service uses identical N254/N62/A58/N665/N666/N669 IDs. The model cannot distinguish a dry tunnel from flooded approaches, village bus dependence, A58/N-road evacuation, vertical refuge, water/drainage control or service-sector edges; 60 GTFS stops provide schedules/locations only.
findings.action: Use monthly CC0 NWB plus event-valid NDW/GTFS/operator data only for mobility/supply reference and live/replay state, with explicit N62 approach/tunnel segments and destinations. Build separate safe aggregate graphs for utilities/facilities; no public reference feed alone establishes evacuation or transfer capacity.

findings.summary: Borssele/Sloe transmission, offshore landing, distribution and vulnerable village assets are absent from the power causal graph.
findings.evidence: Coastal power availability is exactly 0.605326 at T+24 and compound is 0.628130, but no TenneT Borssele 380 kV, Sloe/Nieuwdorp project node, Stedin distribution zone, Hoedekenskerke/Baarland transformer context or authorized switching/restoration interface exists. Project and congestion data are context, not an outage.
findings.action: Ingest annual Stedin SHP and official TenneT/RVO project geometry as versioned context; request authorized safe aggregate dependency/outage/restoration zones. Keep live topology, flows, switching, backups and repair timing unknown when unavailable and never infer them from roads or project plans.

findings.summary: Rural facility, care, shelter and reception continuity is uncalibrated despite large late modeled degradation.
findings.evidence: The public intersection has zero RIVM acute-care locations, 20 DUO education uses and 14 government points, but no shelter/care capacity or live status. Coastal facilities fall from 0.709153 at T+24 to 0.314875 at T+72 and compound to 0.166170 without a named facility, occupancy, generator, supply, staff or transfer plan.
findings.action: Retain RIVM/DUO/KVK/BAG as role/location context only. Request municipality/VRZ-authorized safe aggregate care, reception, shelter, cooling, accessible-transport and continuity interfaces; otherwise keep activation, occupancy, endurance and restoration synthetic/unknown.

findings.summary: The current engine satisfies exact-zero, sustained-water, reconciliation, deterministic and explanation-ledger contracts.
findings.evidence: The focused model gate and reproduction cover 10 presets x 6 checkpoints x 8 services; all 32-row allocations close, layer selection is non-causal, causal ledgers reconcile, public sources show evidence class and affectsSimulation=false, and persistent standing water prevents false recovery.
findings.action: Keep these gates mandatory while adding locally sourced spatial inputs; add regression assertions for named-source connectivity, non-identical hazard ranks, public-context non-causality and explicit unsupported dimensions.

corrections.summary: Replace generic Borsele coastal/river scalars with expert-selected Westerschelde and regional-water exercises.
corrections.validation: Best public integration sources are Scheldestromen EXT_ALG_DSO_2025/EXT_WK ArcGIS reach geometry (full water-board area, EPSG:28992, 2025 edition, public-service licence/cadence unstated), Province Zeeland protected/unprotected depth WMS/WFS (scenario polygons/grids, Public Domain, fixed layer version and refresh cadence unstated), LIWO OGC (named depth/arrival/flow/duration scenarios, layer-specific resolution/version, licence/cadence not established) and Waterinfo observations (location/parameter-specific, often 10-minute). Clip with annual full-resolution CBS geometry (CC BY 4.0). Require event, reach/state, probability, depth unit, CRS, cell size, arrival/recession, issue/valid time, no-data and terms. Until expert approval, mark local direct exposure unsupported; do not infer a present breach from the 16 km strengthening programme.

corrections.summary: Integrate hazard-specific pluvial, heat, drought/salinisation and fire eligibility instead of one neighbourhood seed.
corrections.validation: Ask Gemeente Borsele/Scheldestromen for stable machine exports behind the climate programme with design rain, raster/vector resolution, edition, no-data, cadence and reuse licence; the public 2017 PDF has none and must remain fixed planning evidence. Use PDOK AHN WCS latest 0.5 m mosaic (open-data metadata/licence must be pinned) and daily BGT CC0 surfaces as terrain/impervious covariates, never observed water. Use KNMI Data Platform 5-/10-minute event-valid radar/weather files (CC BY 4.0) only for a named replay. For fire, use current IPO/Risicokaart combustible-area WFS/WMS (Public Domain; metadata cadence, not live incident cadence) as eligibility, not an ignition/perimeter. Test no-data != zero and require different spatial ranks for physically different hazards.

corrections.summary: Add explicitly scoped, authority-reviewed Borssele radiological and Sloe industrial-release exercises or a visible scope exclusion.
corrections.validation: Use national REV WFS/WMS (feature/attention-area resolution, per-record registration/validity, fixed cadence and licence version unstated) only for source/context selection; missing/no-value fields stay unknown. Bind event-valid KNMI wind/precipitation (5-/10-minute products, CC BY 4.0) to a named replay. Use VRZ 2026-2029 and national iodine/shelter/evacuation guidance as fixed policy context, not an automatic decision. No reviewed public API safely supplies KCB/industrial source terms, dose, live plant state, crews or operational protective-action decisions; request authorized authority data or use one smallest named/versioned synthetic exercise with explicit source-term, plume and uncertainty. Assert generic cyber never implies KCB reactor-control failure.

corrections.summary: Represent N62/Westerscheldetunnel approaches, rural evacuation and public transport separately from non-mobility lifelines.
corrections.validation: Use RWS NWB OGC monthly CC0 1.0 (or daily Public Domain GeoPackage) for road segmentation; use timestamped NDW DATEX II observed closures/speeds and feed-valid GTFS/operator schedules for a matched replay. Explicitly model N62 tunnel versus vulnerable approach links, A58/N-roads, village pickups, safe destinations/vertical refuge and emergency access. None of NWB, NDW or GTFS supplies evacuation throughput, vehicle/accessibility stock, contraflow, destination capacity or future T+72 state; obtain authority assumptions or label bounded synthetic values. Remove road IDs from power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/facilities.

corrections.summary: Build service-specific safe aggregate Borsele power, water/drainage, gas, telecom and supply interfaces.
corrections.validation: For power ingest Stedin annual SHP geometry (service area/component resolution, snapshot date in metadata, standard licence unstated and indicative only) plus TenneT/RVO project decisions as fixed context; congestion/project records are not outage or spare-capacity observations. For water/drainage use HWH IMWA/DAMO OGC (object geometry, CC BY-SA 4.0, provider timestamps/variable completeness) and Scheldestromen 2025 ArcGIS context; the current footprint has 116 registered objects, but topology, units, control, live state and backup are not established. No complete public gas, telecom, drinking-water, industrial-stock, switching or restoration feed was verified. residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, emergency instruction, flood assessment, evacuation plan, nuclear/industrial safety case, outage report or operator commitment.
CBS 2025 values are rounded or suppressed; resident population excludes present workers, visitors, school/care occupants and evacuees, and null indicators are unknown rather than zero.
The 148-position overview boundary is suitable for selection, not defence, raster, low-point, road, catchment, plume or asset intersection; use full-resolution annual PDOK geometry.
BAG woonplaats and CBS boundaries are independently versioned; two official label centres fail containment and must not be used to rewrite municipality membership.
The municipal climate quick scan is 2017 fixed expert evidence with no stable machine export, resolution, licence or guaranteed refresh; current local validation is required.
Scheldestromen/HWH defence and water objects are legal/reference context, not current condition, hydraulic connectivity, capacity/control, failure, emergency power or restoration performance.

LIWO/Zeeland depth layers are modeled scenarios and require expert event/version/unit/resolution/probability/no-data/terms selection; Waterinfo/KNMI observations can support a named replay but do not create a generic T+72 flood forecast.

REV activity and attention-area data are regulatory context, not current fire, explosion, toxic/radiological release, plume, damage, probability, dose or protective-action decision; absent records are not zero hazard.
Public VRZ/Rijksoverheid/EPZ pages describe preparedness and scope, not a live KCB state, source term, restricted plan, staffing/resource inventory or response commitment.
NWB, NDW, GTFS and tunnel/operator reference data do not provide future closure, evacuation demand, vehicle/accessibility stock, destination capacity or emergency throughput.

No complete public physical electricity, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom, facility, industrial stock, supply, backup, switching, repair or restoration topology is consumed; unavailable/security-sensitive elements remain unknown or synthetic.
RIVM/DUO/KVK/BAG locations do not establish live occupancy, shelter role, capacity, staffing, accessibility, supplies, generator endurance or patient transfer.
Remote Groningen earthquake and remote wildfire presets are exercises rather than Borsele events; cyber and weather presets are synthetic unless explicitly bound to a versioned replay.

Recovery after T+72, defence project completion, cross-Western-Scheldt effects, Belgian/Doel coordination, seasonal agriculture/recreation and mutual-aid constraints remain outside locally validated model scope.
